title: Harmonic removal couples dip depths in released TESS CPV series from 60 stars
abstract: We test whether separate dips in complex periodic variables (CPVs) deepen together. In 538 selected pairs from 163 star-sector records and 60 stars, the median star correlation is 0.222 (95% interval 0.135 to 0.313). The source removes a constant and two harmonics per rotation. We derive its multi-dip response matrix. A geometry-only prediction correlates with the measured pair correlations at r = 0.682 (0.619 to 0.742). A correction with fixed flat dip profiles changes the median to -0.056 (-0.093 to -0.017). This shift is a processing sensitivity, not a physical covariance estimate. A single changing Gaussian cloud produces three significant residual dip runs with perfectly correlated depths. Known Gaussian inserts give recovered-to-true amplitude correlations of 0.75-0.84 in control stars and 0.61-0.66 in CPV backgrounds. Missing bins and unequal weights can shift synthetic pair correlations by up to 0.22, beyond the corrected empirical signal. Thus these residual depths do not securely measure common material supply. We provide response code, aggregate results, input hashes, known-signal tests and separate-scratch reproduction steps. We infer no material mass, supply rate or lifetime.

display.caption: Measured dip correlations and conditional response correction, with known-template tests. Intervals do not include profile or coverage error.
